subject: Kernel team capacity: senior slate and headcount request for runtime improvements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Kernel team capacity: senior slate and headcount request for runtime improvements

Team —

Quick summary: the Kernel/Runtime squad is requesting approval to open and commit to three senior-level roles focused on improving inference latency, memory behavior for long sequences, and compilation/quantization stability. This is a targeted slate (not an open headcount pool):

- 2x Senior Compiler Engineers (focus: attention kernel optimizations, quantization validation)
- 1x Staff Runtime Engineer (focus: KV cache stability and multi-GPU replication)

Why now:
- Q3 product commitments include low-latency streaming and a 2x increase in seq-length support for a key customer (ACME Media). Without senior hires we will be capacity-constrained and will miss the latency SLO and increased memory-efficiency target.
- Current team velocity shows significant rework cycles tied to edge-case attention patterns that require compiler-level fixes.

Comp bands proposed (base only, ranges pulled from comp-bench):
- Senior Compiler Engineer: $185,000 - $220,000 base
- Staff Runtime Engineer: $255,000 - $300,000 base
- Target OTE (est): Senior: $230-275k, Staff: $320-360k (includes equity and bonus)

Financial ask:
- Headcount additions: 3 FTEs (one-time ramp over next 6-10 weeks to offers accepted)
- FY26 incremental run-rate (salary + benefits + hiring costs): approx $780k - $920k

Attachments: kernel-slate-budget.xlsx, comp-band-comparison.pdf (detailed band comps and run-rate).

Requested decision: approval to post and extend offers up to the top of the bands above. If approval is granted, recruiting will prioritize ACME-aligned tenure and low-risk profile candidates to shorten time-to-offer.

Next steps I propose:
1) Approve the 3 headcount and comp bands, or approve a partial hire plan (we can prioritize 2 hires now).
2) We’ll present a short hiring/recruiting plan to Finance and Recruiting within 48 hours if approved.

Appreciate direction—this is blocking several Q3 milestones.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Platform & Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: kernel-slate-budget.xlsx (spreadsheet), comp-band-comparison.pdf (PDF)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kernel team capacity: senior slate and headcount request for runtime improvements

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying asks before I take to Finance for headcount release: 

1) Can you confirm the expected time-to-hire per role (recruiter estimate), and the earliest realistic start dates?
2) The run-rate number looks like a band — can you give a midpoint run-rate and a worst-case assume-top-of-band run-rate so Finance can model?
3) If we can only get approval for 2 hires now, which two should we prioritize and what’s the specific risk/impact for delaying the third by one quarter?

If you can answer this in-line I’ll prepare the headcount release note.

-k

Subject: Re: Kernel team capacity: senior slate and headcount request for runtime improvements

Kimberly — answers below. I updated the budget spreadsheet (kernel-slate-budget-v2.xlsx) to include midpoint and top-of-band run-rate assumptions.

1) Recruiter estimate / timeline:
- Senior Compiler Engineer: 6-9 weeks to offer (we have two inbound profiles from referrals), earliest realistic start: mid-June 2026.
- Staff Runtime Engineer: 8-10 weeks to offer, earliest realistic start: late-June / early-July 2026.

2) Run-rate: (salaries + 30% benefits/hiring overhead) — numbers use midpoint / top-of-band bases:
- 2x Senior (midpoint): $410k base total -> $533k with benefits/hiring overhead
- 1x Staff (midpoint): $275k base -> $357.5k with benefits/hiring overhead
- Combined midpoint run-rate: ~$890.5k
- Top-of-band combined run-rate: ~$1.02M

3) If limited to 2 hires now — recommended priority:
- Hire 1 Staff Runtime Engineer + 1 Senior Compiler Engineer.
- Impact of delaying the 2nd Senior: slower progress on attention-kernel regressions; some features (notably long-sequence streaming) get deprioritized and could slip one quarter. We keep customer-facing latency work but lose parallelization on the quantization stability project which increases risk on certain open-source model variants.

I’ve attached kernel-slate-budget-v2.xlsx (updated) for Finance modeling. Recruiters can start outreach as soon as we get approval to post.

Marissa

--
Attachment stub: kernel-slate-budget-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kernel team capacity: senior slate and headcount request for runtime improvements

Thanks for the clear ask and the updated numbers. I’m prepared to grant conditional approval as follows: 

- Approve hiring for 2 roles immediately: 1x Staff Runtime Engineer and 1x Senior Compiler Engineer.
- Approve a headcount hold for the 3rd senior compiler slot pending Q3 budget review (Finance will need a firm hiring plan and expected candidate profiles).
- Condition: Recruiting plan + two candidate scorecards must be provided to Finance and Naomi within 72 hours of posting. If recruiting demonstrates strong pipeline (2+ viable candidates per role within 4 weeks) we will greenlight the third hire without another exec cycle.

Please proceed with posting and prioritize referral and passive sourcing channels. Naomi — please coordinate the headcount release and let Recruiting know the conditions.

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
